keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «늑대가 돌아오자 엘크가 움직이며 강가의 나무가 다시 자라기 시작했다(변화)» 와 «먹이 사슬의 모든 생물은 꼭대기에 있는 생물까지 서로에게 기대어 산다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the change (when the wolves returned, the elk moved around more, so trees started to grow back) and the conclusion (every living thing in a food chain depends on the others). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why did the trees near the rivers start to grow back?
qs.qko: 강가의 나무들이 다시 자라기 시작한 이유는 무엇인가요?
opts: Because the elk moved around more and avoided some open river areas
Because scientists planted new trees every day
Because beavers chased the elk away
evs: The elk began to move around more and avoid some open river areas, so trees there started to grow back.
Without them, the number of elk, a kind of large deer, had grown very large.
It usually starts with plants, called producers, which make their own food from sunlight.
In 1995, scientists released a small group of gray wolves into Yellowstone National Park in the United States.
why: 늑대가 돌아오자 엘크가 더 많이 돌아다니며 탁 트인 강가 일부를 피했고, 그래서 그곳 나무가 다시 자라기 시작했다고 했어요.
When the wolves returned, the elk moved around more and avoided some open river areas, so trees there started to grow back.

qs.q: In "the trees could hardly grow," what does "hardly" mean?
qs.qko: «the trees could hardly grow» 에서 «hardly» 는 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: The elk ate so many young trees near the rivers that the trees could hardly grow.
In Yellowstone, one chain was simple: trees, then elk, then wolves.
Yellowstone shows that every living thing in a food chain depends on the others, even the ones at the top.
Wolves had disappeared from the park about 70 years earlier.
why: 엘크가 어린 나무를 너무 많이 먹었으니, 나무가 «거의 자라지 못했다» 는 뜻이에요. «hardly» 는 «거의 ~않다» 예요.
The elk ate so many young trees, so «hardly» means the trees almost could not grow.

qs.q: In Yellowstone’s simple food chain, which living thing makes its own food from sunlight?
qs.qko: 옐로스톤의 단순한 먹이 사슬에서 햇빛으로 스스로 양분을 만드는 생물은 무엇인가요?
opts: The trees, because plants are producers that make food from sunlight
The wolves, because they are at the top of the chain
The elk, because they eat young trees
evs: In Yellowstone, one chain was simple: trees, then elk, then wolves.
Wolves had disappeared from the park about 70 years earlier.
It usually starts with plants, called producers, which make their own food from sunlight.
When the wolves returned, something surprising happened.
why: 옐로스톤의 먹이 사슬은 나무 → 엘크 → 늑대 순서이고, 먹이 사슬은 햇빛으로 스스로 양분을 만드는 생산자인 식물에서 시작한다고 했어요. 두 문장을 이으면 답이 나무라는 것을 알 수 있어요.
Yellowstone’s chain is trees, then elk, then wolves, and a food chain starts with plants, the producers that make their own food from sunlight. Together, they show the answer is the trees.

write.howtoEn: Use the example as a pattern. Write a condition and what we can do then in English.

write.moreKo: 한 걸음 더: «If» 뒤에 «누가 + 무엇을 하는지» 를 넣어 조건을 분명하게 써 보세요. (예: If we plant more trees)
